title: Dr. Andrew Huberman: The Real Function of the Amygdala and Anxiety Control
transcript_text: Heard about the amygdala for its role in anxiety and fear and threat detection. And indeed, the amygdala is part of the network in the brain that generates feelings of fear and threat and anxiety. It does a bunch of other things too. It's involved in positive anticipation. But when the amygdala is active, we feel agitation and a desire to move and change our state.
